basic_information.name: Devin
basic_information.creator: Cognition Labs (also known as Cognition AI), founded by Scott Wu (CEO), Steven Hao (CTO), and Walden Yan (CPO) in August 2023. All three founders are IOI gold medalists. The 10-person founding team collectively holds 10 IOI gold medals.
basic_information.release_date: March 12, 2024 (initial announcement and preview); Devin 2.0 launched April 3, 2025; Devin 2.1 released mid-2025 with confidence scores
basic_information.current_version: Devin 2.1 (as of February 2026), with continuous updates — latest release notes from February 3, 2026. Now powered by Claude Sonnet 4.5 (previously GPT-4 at launch).

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: single_agent — Devin operates as a single autonomous agent running in a cloud-based sandboxed VM. Each Devin instance has its own isolated environment with shell, code editor, and browser. Multiple Devin instances can be spun up in parallel, but each operates independently rather than as collaborating agents.
technical_architecture.underlying_models: Originally powered by OpenAI GPT-4 at launch (March 2024). Cognition rebuilt Devin for Claude Sonnet 4.5 (Anthropic) in late 2025, reporting 2x faster execution and 12% improvement on Junior Developer Evals. The system also includes a new 'Devin Agent Preview' variant. Data Analyst Devin (Dana) is a specialized variant optimized for data analysis tasks. Cognition has proprietary fine-tuning and orchestration layers on top of the base models.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: Devin operates within a sandboxed VM equipped with: (1) Shell/terminal for running commands, (2) Code editor for file modifications, (3) Web browser for research and interaction. External integrations include: GitHub (PR creation, code review, CI monitoring), GitLab (beta), Jira, Linear (with confidence score integration), Slack. MCP (Model Context Protocol) support via MCP Marketplace, supporting stdio, SSE, and HTTP transport methods, giving access to hundreds of external tools and data sources. Also integrates with DeepWiki for automatic documentation generation.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: Interactive Planning — Devin 2.0 introduced a collaborative planning system. Upon starting a session, Devin automatically analyzes the codebase, identifies relevant files, and proposes an initial plan within seconds, even without specific instructions. Developers can refine the plan before execution begins. Devin 2.1 added Confidence Scores that indicate task completion likelihood, pausing for user approval when confidence is not green. This is a hybrid approach combining autonomous code analysis with human-in-the-loop refinement.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: Not a multi-agent framework per se. Multiple independent Devin instances can run in parallel (each in its own VM), but they do not communicate or collaborate with each other. Goldman Sachs deployed hundreds of Devin instances simultaneously. The architecture is 'multi-instance single-agent' rather than true multi-agent orchestration.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: short_term (conversation within a session), semantic (codebase knowledge via Devin Search and Devin Wiki features introduced in 2.0), procedural (Devin learns from past sessions and mistakes — the 2025 performance review noted it 'learns from its mistakes over time'). Devin Search indexes the full codebase for semantic retrieval. Devin Wiki automatically generates documentation about the codebase.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: Devin uses codebase-aware retrieval: upon starting a session, it automatically scans and indexes the repository to identify relevant files. Devin Search provides semantic search across the codebase. The underlying Claude Sonnet 4.5 model provides a large context window. Cognition's proprietary orchestration layer manages context across long-running tasks.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: cloud — Each Devin session runs in a cloud-based VM. Session state, audit logs, and work history persist in Cognition's cloud infrastructure. Enterprise VPC deployment available for data isolation. Pull requests and audit logs of all research and work are created at task completion.
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Context is treated as a first-class concern. Devin 2.0 introduced three context-related features: (1) Interactive Planning — proactively analyzes codebase to build context before execution, (2) Devin Search — semantic search across the full codebase for on-demand context retrieval, (3) Devin Wiki — automatically generated documentation providing persistent codebase context. The system reads AGENTS.md files for project-specific instructions.

capabilities.core_capabilities: Devin is positioned as 'the first AI software engineer' — an autonomous coding agent capable of end-to-end software development tasks. Core capabilities include: (1) Writing code from specifications and natural language descriptions, (2) Bug investigation, diagnosis, and fixing with CI test verification, (3) Pull request creation and code review, (4) Code migrations and refactoring (batch edits feature for repetitive refactors), (5) Building web applications from scratch, (6) Responding to on-call issues, (7) Data analysis via Dana (Data Analyst Devin), (8) Interactive codebase exploration via Devin Search and Devin Wiki, (9) Browsing the web for research and documentation, (10) Learning from mistakes over time. Performance metrics (2025 review): 4x faster at problem solving vs. prior year, 2x more efficient in resource consumption, 67% PR merge rate (up from 34%), hundreds of thousands of PRs merged across thousands of companies. Excels at tasks with clear requirements that would take a junior engineer 4-8 hours. SWE-bench: resolved 13.86% of real GitHub issues (7x improvement over prior best unassisted model at 1.96%). Devin 2.0 completes 83% more junior-level dev tasks per ACU vs. predecessor.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Text, code (multi-language), browser (web browsing and interaction), file system (within sandboxed VM), shell/terminal. No native voice or image generation capabilities, though can process screenshots via browser.
capabilities.autonomy_level: autonomous (with human-in-loop option) — Devin operates autonomously by default, but Devin 2.1 introduced confidence-based escalation: when confidence score is green, it proceeds automatically; when not green, it waits for user approval. Users can step in at any point to review, edit, or guide progress. Goldman Sachs frames it as 'a new employee' that works alongside human engineers.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: Extensive and growing: GitHub integration (PRs, issues, CI), GitLab (beta), Jira, Linear, Slack, MCP Marketplace (hundreds of external tools via Model Context Protocol supporting stdio/SSE/HTTP transports), web browser, shell, code editor. DeepWiki for documentation. Enterprise integrations include SSO, VPC deployment. The Windsurf acquisition (July 2025) brings additional IDE capabilities and 350+ enterprise customers.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: Full MCP support. Devin has an MCP Marketplace where users can connect Devin to any MCP server. Supports 3 transport methods: stdio, SSE, and HTTP. Additionally, there is a Devin MCP Server (open-source, available on GitHub) that allows other AI agents to delegate tasks to Devin via MCP.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: No explicit A2A (Agent-to-Agent Protocol) support documented as of February 2026. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: Yes — Devin reads and respects AGENTS.md files placed in the project root. AGENTS.md has been adopted by 60,000+ open-source projects and is supported by Devin alongside Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and VS Code.
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: Devin is primarily a standalone product rather than a framework, so cross-framework compatibility is limited. However, MCP support provides broad interoperability with any MCP-compatible tool or service. The Devin MCP Server allows other agents/frameworks to delegate tasks to Devin. The Windsurf acquisition adds IDE-level integration capabilities. No native integration with frameworks like LangChain, AutoGen, or CrewAI.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: sandbox — Each Devin instance runs in an isolated sandboxed VM with its own shell, editor, and browser. Enterprise deployments support VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) for complete data isolation. Administrators can review and manage all permissions granted to Devin. Customer data is stored within the customer's tenant for enterprise deployments. SOC 2 Type II certified (September 2024).
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Confidence-based escalation (Devin 2.1): Devin provides Confidence Scores indicating likelihood of task completion. When confidence is green, Devin proceeds automatically. When confidence is not green, Devin pauses and waits for user approval before proceeding. Users can also step in at any point during execution to review, edit, or redirect. Integration with Jira and Linear allows batch confidence scoring for multiple issues.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Multiple strategies: (1) Sandboxed execution — code is actually run and tested, not just generated, catching hallucinated logic, (2) CI integration — Devin verifies fixes pass continuous integration tests, (3) Interactive Planning — humans review and approve plans before execution begins, (4) Confidence Scores — Devin self-assesses completion likelihood, escalating uncertain tasks, (5) Audit trail — full session logs enable human review of all reasoning and actions. However, Devin is still a junior-level system and 'can't independently tackle an ambiguous coding project end-to-end like a senior engineer could.'
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: Yes — Devin creates a Pull Request and an audit log of all its research, reasoning, and work for every task. Developers can review the complete session including all browser searches, terminal commands, and code changes.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: confidence_threshold — Devin 2.1 uses confidence scores to determine when to proceed autonomously (green confidence) vs. when to pause for human approval (non-green confidence). Users can also intervene at any time. The Interactive Planning feature provides pre-approval of task plans before execution. This is a hybrid model combining confidence-based automation with always-available human override.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: None — Devin is a proprietary product by Cognition Labs, not governed by any standards body. However, Cognition participates in the broader AI coding ecosystem: supports MCP (Anthropic-originated, now standardized), AGENTS.md (community standard adopted by 60,000+ projects).
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: Supports and implements: Model Context Protocol (MCP) with full marketplace, AGENTS.md standard for project-level agent instructions. Offers Devin MCP Server as an open-source contribution allowing other agents to delegate tasks to Devin.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: SOC2 Type II certified (September 2024, verified by third-party auditors). Enterprise features include: VPC deployment for complete data isolation, SSO (Single Sign-On), access control, customer data stored within customer tenant. HIPAA, GDPR, and EU AI Act compliance not explicitly documented. [uncertain]

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: cloud | managed_service — Devin is primarily a cloud-hosted SaaS product. Enterprise plan offers VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) deployment for complete data isolation. No local/on-premise or edge deployment options available.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: horizontal — Multiple Devin instances can be spun up in parallel, each in its own isolated VM. Goldman Sachs deployed hundreds of instances with plans to scale to thousands. Enterprise plan supports parallel capabilities with dedicated support.
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: Pricing is based on Agent Compute Units (ACUs). 1 ACU ≈ 15 minutes of active Devin work. Core plan: $2.25/ACU (minimum $20/month for 9 ACUs). Team plan: $2.00/ACU ($500/month for 250 ACUs, additional ACUs at $2/each). Enterprise: custom pricing. Effective hourly rate: ~$9-11/hour of AI labor. For reference, 1 ACU can handle tasks like: finding an old commit and restoring a feature, investigating and fixing a bug with CI verification, or creating a simple personal website.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: No local hardware requirements — Devin runs entirely in Cognition's cloud infrastructure (sandboxed VMs). Users interact via web browser. Enterprise VPC deployment may have additional infrastructure requirements (not publicly documented).

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: Devin provides built-in session monitoring: real-time progress reporting within the Devin IDE, Slack notifications for task updates, integration with Jira and Linear for issue tracking and confidence scoring. No documented integration with third-party observability tools like LangSmith, Langfuse, or Datadog. [uncertain]
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Yes — Full audit trail of every Devin session including all browser searches, terminal commands, code edits, and reasoning steps. Developers can review the complete session trace after task completion.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: production_ready — Devin is used in production by thousands of companies including Goldman Sachs, Santander, Nubank, Cisco, Palantir, and Mercado Libre. SOC 2 Type II certified. ARR grew from $1M (September 2024) to $73M (June 2025). Combined with Windsurf, the platform has 350+ enterprise customers and hundreds of thousands of daily active users.

adoption_and_market.github_stars: N/A — Devin is proprietary/closed-source. However, the open-source alternative OpenDevin (now OpenHands) has 20,700+ GitHub stars. The Devin MCP Server has separate open-source repos (kazuph/mcp-devin and desertaxle/devin-mcp).
adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: ARR: $1M (September 2024) → $73M (June 2025). Combined ARR after Windsurf acquisition doubled, with enterprise ARR up 30%+ post-acquisition. Windsurf brought $82M ARR and 350+ enterprise customers. Hundreds of thousands of daily active users (Windsurf). Thousands of companies use Devin in their engineering teams. Notable customers: Goldman Sachs, Santander, Nubank, Cisco, Palantir, Mercado Libre. Hundreds of thousands of PRs merged. Goldman Sachs deployed hundreds of Devin instances with plans for thousands.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: Freemium / tiered SaaS: Core plan at $20/month (9 ACUs), Team plan at $500/month (250 ACUs), Enterprise at custom pricing. Pay-as-you-go ACU model ($2.00-$2.25/ACU). Originally launched at $500/month flat rate before Devin 2.0 price reduction in April 2025.
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: Primary use cases: (1) Software engineering task automation — bug fixes, feature implementation, code refactoring for tasks that would take a junior engineer 4-8 hours, (2) Code migrations and large-scale refactoring (batch edits), (3) Pull request creation and code review, (4) On-call incident response, (5) Data analysis (via Dana), (6) Web application development, (7) CI/CD pipeline support. Industries: Financial services (Goldman Sachs, Santander, Nubank — risk, compliance, data engineering), technology (Cisco, Palantir), e-commerce (Mercado Libre). Goldman Sachs estimates Devin could handle 20-40% of software engineering workload.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: Devin occupies a unique position as the most autonomous AI coding agent on the market — positioned as a 'virtual junior engineer' rather than a coding copilot. Key differentiators: (1) Fully autonomous execution in sandboxed VMs vs. IDE-integrated copilots, (2) End-to-end task completion (research → code → PR → CI), (3) Parallelizable (multiple instances). Competitors: Cursor ($10B valuation, 50% Fortune 500 adoption, IDE-based copilot), GitHub Copilot (most widely adopted, Microsoft/GitHub ecosystem), Claude Code (Anthropic, CLI-based), Amazon Q Developer, Augment Code. After Windsurf acquisition, Cognition covers both autonomous agent (Devin) and agentic IDE (Windsurf) segments. Cognition valued at $10.2B (September 2025), making it one of the most valuable AI coding companies.

ecosystem_maturity.community_size: Cognition does not maintain a public open-source community for Devin itself (proprietary product). The broader ecosystem includes: OpenDevin/OpenHands (open-source alternative, 20.7K GitHub stars, active community with Discord and Slack), Devika (open-source Devin alternative on GitHub). Cognition has a Trust Center and enterprise support channels. DeepWiki (free for open-source) has indexed 50,000+ GitHub repos. Cognition team includes ~100+ employees post-Windsurf acquisition. [uncertain]
ecosystem_maturity.documentation_quality: good — Official documentation at docs.devin.ai covers onboarding, release notes, enterprise security, MCP marketplace, and AGENTS.md support. Release notes are regularly published. Blog posts on cognition.ai provide technical depth (e.g., Claude Sonnet 4.5 migration lessons, annual performance reviews). However, as a proprietary product, deep technical architecture details are limited compared to open-source alternatives.
ecosystem_maturity.third_party_integrations_count: Substantial: GitHub, GitLab (beta), Jira, Linear, Slack, MCP Marketplace (hundreds of tools via MCP servers), SSO providers, VPC deployment infrastructure. Post-Windsurf acquisition, additional IDE integrations. Exact count not publicly disclosed but MCP alone provides access to hundreds of external tools.
ecosystem_maturity.tutorial_availability: Moderate — Official docs provide getting-started guides and onboarding materials. Cognition blog has technical posts and use case examples. Numerous third-party reviews, comparisons, and tutorials on Medium, Dev.to, YouTube. No official certification program or structured course. Community-created content is growing rapidly given Devin's viral attention.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: autonomous — Devin acts independently on tasks with green confidence scores, executing end-to-end from planning through PR creation. Escalates to human approval when confidence is non-green. Users can intervene at any time. Goldman Sachs treats it as 'a new employee' — autonomous but supervised. More autonomous than copilot-style tools (Cursor, Copilot) but not fully_delegated — still requires human review of PRs and can be redirected mid-task.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Multi-modal handoff: (1) Confidence Score system — Devin pauses and presents its plan when confidence is non-green, waiting for human approval, (2) Real-time progress reporting — users can observe Devin's work and intervene at any point via the IDE interface, (3) Pull Request review — all completed work is submitted as PRs for human review before merging, (4) Slack integration — Devin reports progress and can receive feedback via Slack, (5) Interactive Planning — humans can refine Devin's proposed plan before execution begins.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Devin learns from its mistakes over time (noted in 2025 performance review). PR merge rates improved from 34% to 67% year-over-year, suggesting the system incorporates feedback. Interactive Planning allows real-time plan refinement based on human input. The Confidence Score system is itself a feedback mechanism — Devin calibrates its self-assessment based on task outcomes. Specific technical details of the learning/feedback architecture are not publicly disclosed (proprietary).

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: High relevance for startup founders: (1) WHEN TO USE: Devin is ideal for startups that need to extend limited engineering capacity — it can handle junior-level tasks (bug fixes, migrations, simple features, code reviews) at ~$9-11/hour, far cheaper than hiring. Goldman Sachs estimates 20-40% of engineering workload could shift to tools like Devin. Startups can spin up multiple Devin instances for parallel task execution. (2) WHEN TO AVOID: Not suitable for core architecture decisions, ambiguous requirements, or tasks requiring senior-level judgment. Devin excels at well-specified 4-8 hour tasks, not open-ended product strategy. Startups should not rely on Devin for security-critical or compliance-sensitive code without thorough human review. (3) COST CONSIDERATION: At $20/month (Core) to $500/month (Team), it's extremely affordable compared to developer salaries. However, ACU costs can add up for heavy usage — budget carefully. (4) STRATEGIC CONTEXT: The Windsurf acquisition signals Cognition's ambition to own the full developer toolchain (autonomous agent + IDE). Startups building on Devin should consider platform lock-in risk. The $10.2B valuation and $73M+ ARR suggest strong market traction and continued investment.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: BUY Devin for operational engineering tasks (bug fixes, migrations, code reviews, simple features). BUILD custom AI workflows only if: (1) your core product IS an AI coding tool, (2) you need deep integration with proprietary systems that MCP doesn't cover, (3) you require full control over the underlying model and inference pipeline. For most startups, Devin at $20-500/month is far more cost-effective than building autonomous coding agents from scratch. Alternatives to consider: Cursor ($20/month) for copilot-style IDE assistance, GitHub Copilot ($10-19/month) for lightweight autocompletion, Claude Code for CLI-based development. Devin's unique value is autonomy — it works independently while you focus on other things, unlike copilots that require continuous human interaction.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 5 (Ethics, governance & final presentations) — Devin raises important questions about AI replacing junior engineering roles (Goldman Sachs 'new employee' framing). Also relevant to Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects) for build-vs-buy decisions and Session 4 (AI business models & strategy) as a case study in AI product pricing (from $500 flat to $20 ACU-based model) and hypergrowth ($1M to $73M ARR in 9 months).

confidence.data_quality: High — Information sourced from Cognition's official blog, TechCrunch, VentureBeat, CNBC, Bloomberg, Fortune, IBM Think, official documentation (docs.devin.ai), and enterprise case studies (Goldman Sachs). ARR and valuation figures confirmed across multiple tier-1 business publications.
confidence.cross_reference: Multiple sources confirm key data points: (1) $10.2B valuation — TechCrunch, CNBC, Bloomberg, (2) $73M ARR — Cognition blog, multiple tech publications, (3) Goldman Sachs adoption — IBM Think, TechCrunch, Fortune, FastCompany, (4) Windsurf acquisition at ~$250M — TechCrunch, CNBC, (5) SWE-bench 13.86% — Cognition technical report, (6) Pricing structure — official devin.ai/pricing, TechCrunch, VentureBeat.
confidence.caveats: Key caveats: (1) Rapidly evolving — Devin releases updates frequently (latest February 3, 2026), features and pricing may change, (2) SWE-bench 13.86% was the original benchmark; independent testing shows 15-30% in practice — still limited for complex tasks, (3) 'Junior engineer' framing is Cognition's own positioning — real-world performance varies by task complexity, (4) Windsurf integration is still ongoing — the combined product strategy is evolving, (5) Some Windsurf staff were offered exit doors 3 weeks post-acquisition (TechCrunch), suggesting integration challenges, (6) The $10.2B valuation is based on rapid ARR growth but the AI coding market is intensely competitive with well-funded rivals (Cursor at $10B, GitHub Copilot backed by Microsoft), (7) Underlying model dependency — switching from GPT-4 to Claude Sonnet 4.5 shows model risk; future model changes could affect performance.
